Re: Demand for Payment — Unpaid Invoices under Purchase Order NM-2024-0118
Our Client: Larkspur Timber Supply LLC

Dear Ms. Raghavan:

This firm represents Larkspur Timber Supply LLC ("Larkspur") in connection with amounts owed by Northgate Millwork Company ("Northgate") under Purchase Order NM-2024-0118 dated January 18, 2025 (the "Purchase Order"). This letter is a demand for payment. It is written without prejudice to any of Larkspur's rights and remedies, all of which are expressly reserved.

STATEMENT OF FACTS

On January 18, 2025, Northgate issued the Purchase Order to Larkspur for 184,000 board feet of kiln-dried white oak, to be delivered in six monthly lots between February and July 2025 at a unit price of $4.85 per board foot. The Purchase Order incorporates Larkspur's standard terms of sale, which require payment within thirty (30) days of invoice and provide for interest at 1.5% per month on past-due amounts.

Larkspur delivered all six lots on schedule. Northgate accepted every delivery without objection and did not reject any lot or give notice of any nonconformity within the ten-day inspection period the Purchase Order allows. Northgate paid the first three invoices in full and on time.

Northgate has not paid invoices 4, 5, and 6, which were issued on May 30, June 27, and July 29, 2025, in the amounts of $148,632.50, $151,980.00, and $147,296.25. Those invoices became due on June 29, July 27, and August 28, 2025. The aggregate unpaid principal is $447,908.75.

On October 2, 2025, and again on January 15, 2026, Larkspur's controller wrote to Northgate's accounts payable department requesting payment. Northgate did not respond to either letter. On March 4, 2026, Ms. Raghavan told Larkspur's president by telephone that the invoices were "in the queue." No payment has been received.

LEGAL BASIS

Northgate's failure to pay is a breach of contract under the Purchase Order and the incorporated terms of sale. Larkspur is entitled to the unpaid price under section 2-709 of the Illinois Uniform Commercial Code, 810 ILCS 5/2-709, because Northgate accepted the goods and has not paid the price as it became due. Larkspur is also entitled to contractual interest at 1.5% per month, which through August 14, 2026, totals $79,143.66, and to its reasonable attorney's fees under the fee-shifting provision in section 11 of the terms of sale.

DEMAND

Larkspur demands payment of $527,052.41, consisting of $447,908.75 in unpaid principal and $79,143.66 in accrued contractual interest, on or before September 5, 2026 — twenty-one (21) days from the date of this letter. Payment must be made by wire transfer to the account identified in the enclosed remittance instructions. Interest continues to accrue at 1.5% per month until payment is received in full.

If Northgate disputes any portion of this amount, Northgate must state the basis for the dispute in writing, with supporting documentation, by the same date. Larkspur will consider a reasonable written payment schedule if Northgate proposes one before the deadline, but the existence of discussions does not extend the deadline or suspend the accrual of interest.

If payment is not received and no written dispute is submitted by September 5, 2026, Larkspur has instructed this firm to file suit in the Circuit Court of Cook County, Illinois, seeking the unpaid price, contractual interest, attorney's fees, and costs.

RESERVATION OF RIGHTS

Nothing in this letter is, or may be construed as, a waiver, release, or modification of any right, claim, remedy, or defense available to Larkspur, whether under the Purchase Order, the terms of sale, the Uniform Commercial Code, or otherwise, all of which are expressly reserved. This letter is not a complete statement of the facts or of Larkspur's legal position, and Larkspur reserves the right to assert additional claims and to seek additional or different relief. This letter is written for settlement purposes and is inadmissible to prove liability under Illinois Rule of Evidence 408.

Please direct any response to me at the address above or at dtsukamoto@halloran-tsukamoto.com. If Northgate is represented by counsel in this matter, please have counsel contact me directly.
